title: Review and retrospective gaps park as drafts; triage promotes one only when it names the fitness test it blocks
goal: The sprint review (kb/_self/backlog.md Sprints step 4, .claude/skills/kb-sprint/SKILL.md review step 5) files a gap as a bug in this sprint only when it is S1; every other gap and every retrospective finding is filed as a draft in no sprint with a parked link naming the review or close that found it, under its epic or none; /kb-backlog triage and /kb-sprint plan commit a parked draft to a sprint only with a notes line naming the fitness test of EP-gzr4mmkm it blocks (the held-out rate, the content sprint) or a real user's report; a parked draft that names neither stays a draft and is listed, never promoted; the new rule is a tested question of kb/_self's lookup_eval.csv (what happens to a gap the sprint review finds) that python3 _tools/rag.py eval --root _self answers from backlog.md; and the commit names the failure it answers: a backlog of 106 live items and about 500 item files in 10 days, grown by the review rule every gap becomes a bug

gates.question: How is a parked review gap marked?
options: a draft in no sprint with a parked link naming the review that found it (no new state or tool change)
a new parked status in backlog.py, with list --status parked
a draft under one Parked epic
gates.recommendation: a draft in no sprint with a parked link naming the review that found it (no new state or tool change)
gates.answer: a draft in no sprint with a parked link naming the review that found it (no new state or tool change)

gates.question: What link text marks a parked draft?

notes: Premise run 2026-10-08 (plan step 6): the rule is live text, kb/_self/backlog.md:225 (every gap becomes a bug, in this sprint if it is S1, else in the backlog) and .claude/skills/kb-sprint/SKILL.md review step 5; git log --diff-filter=A on kb/_self/backlog/*.json shows 375 of 501 item-adding commits are chore(backlog): file ..., most named file the SP-... review's gaps. Reproduces. Checks pass before the work by design (precheck 2026-10-08): rag.py eval --root _self pins every tested rule question and runs over the new row once it exists (eval has no per-row selection; the row's id in the eval output is the proof the review reads); backlog.py check and selfdoc.py check pin that the docs and items stay consistent after the rule change. The behaviour change is in prose rules the skills read, so no check can fail before it.
